definitions.explanation: An unexpected meeting or encounter, often with something unpleasant, dangerous, or noteworthy. Carries a stronger, more dramatic nuance than simply meeting someone.

examples.japanese: {熊|くま}に{遭遇|そうぐう}した。
{思|おも}いがけない{場面|ばめん}に{遭遇|そうぐう}して{驚|おどろ}いた。
examples.english: I was surprised to come across an unexpected scene.

examples.japanese: {登山中|とざんちゅう}に{激|はげ}しい{雷雨|らいう}に{遭遇|そうぐう}し、{一時|いちじ}{避難|ひなん}を{余儀|よぎ}なくされた。
examples.english: We encountered a severe thunderstorm while climbing and were forced to take temporary shelter.

notes:
USAGE:
{遭遇|そうぐう} typically implies an unexpected or dramatic encounter. It is often used with unpleasant or dangerous situations (wild animals, storms, accidents), but can also describe unexpected positive encounters.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- に{遭遇|そうぐう}する (to encounter/run into...)
- との{遭遇|そうぐう} (encounter with...)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {事故|じこ}に{遭遇|そうぐう}する (to encounter an accident)
- {野生|やせい}{動物|どうぶつ}に{遭遇|そうぐう}する (to encounter a wild animal)
- {偶然|ぐうぜん}の{遭遇|そうぐう} (chance encounter)
- {遭遇|そうぐう}{戦|せん} (chance battle, encounter battle)

SIMILAR WORDS:
{出会|であ}う is the neutral, everyday word for meeting or encountering. {遭遇|そうぐう} is more formal and dramatic, often implying surprise or danger.
